classifier_rationale: The cardholder handed her card to her daughter to shop, so the charge was made by an authorized user; spending more than the cardholder expected is not a billing error.

retrieved.text: Quality disputes (claims and defenses). A complaint about the quality of goods the cardholder accepted isn't a billing error. It may qualify as a claim against the issuer if the cardholder tried in good faith to resolve it with the merchant, the purchase was over $50, and it happened in the cardholder's state or within 100 miles of their address. The $50 and location limits don't apply when the merchant and issuer are related.

Fraud routing. Any charge the cardholder says they didn't make or authorize goes to the fraud team on the same call. Block the card, reissue, open a fraud claim. Agents do not open these as billing disputes only.

What counts as a billing error. A charge the cardholder didn't authorize; a charge that isn't identified properly; goods or services not accepted or not delivered as agreed; a payment or credit not posted properly; a computational error by the issuer; a request for clarification or documentation about a charge; failure to send a statement to the last known address.

note: Cardholder Patricia Lowell disputes a $318.75 charge at Juniper & Vine Apparel dated 2026-09-23. She gave the physical card to her teenage daughter for back-to-school clothes, expecting about two shirts and pants under $300. The daughter made the purchase and returned the card the same day. The cardholder says nobody else used the card. The cardholder has not contacted the merchant. The daughter removed the tags and refuses to return the items. No quality defect is reported. No billing dispute opened. Not routed to fraud, since the cardholder authorized the card use. Next action: RESOLVE_ON_CALL (explain the charge or provide documentation). Unknown: statement date, whether written notice was sent.
